maps.title: Below the fortress, the roots
paragraphs: The lower caverns led towards Belak and the Gulthias Tree, where the mystery of the strange apples took root. What looked like a local harvest carried a danger that could spread far beyond Oakhurst.

maps.title: Oakhurst, where people waited
paragraphs: Oakhurst awaited news of the missing Hucreles. The company returned from the Citadel with their rings and a warning about twig blights.

maps.title: The fortress beneath Oakhurst
paragraphs: The company descended through these passages while searching for the missing Hucreles. Below Oakhurst, it first encountered the history of Ashardalon.

maps.title: A fortress imagined in stone
paragraphs: The illustration depicts a dwarven fortress in stone. It accompanies the search for Durgeddin’s legacy in the fallen hold of Khundrukar.

maps.title: A mark upon the Stone Tooth
paragraphs: The marked mountain map pointed towards Khundrukar. Orc defences and Durgeddin’s lost works lay beneath the Stone Tooth.

maps.title: Khundrukar · The Black Lake
paragraphs: Nightscale waited in the water at the bottom of the company’s descent. The young black dragon fell here, ending the deepest threat of the Forge of Fury journey.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Khundrukar · The Foundry
paragraphs: Other smiths worked among the remnants of Durgeddin’s halls. The company’s descent through Khundrukar passed these contested forges before the Black Lake.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Khundrukar · The Glitterhame, full plan
paragraphs: The Glitterhame opened beneath the upper halls in caverns of water, fungus and scattered light. The company continued through this deeper country on the way to Nightscale’s lake.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Khundrukar · The Mountain Door
paragraphs: The Mountain Door guarded the way into Durgeddin’s ruined stronghold. Beyond it lay the passages where the company found the twins and arranged their escape.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Khundrukar · The Sinkhole
paragraphs: The Sinkhole belongs to the deeper routes beneath Khundrukar. Its plan connects the upper dungeon’s descent with the lower reaches of the Forge of Fury.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Khundrukar, spread before them
paragraphs: This plan connects the hold’s approaches, forge and waters below. The company descended through them to Nightscale’s lair.

maps.title: The Glitterhame
paragraphs: Water and fungi filled the Glitterhame beneath Khundrukar. The company crossed its caverns on the way towards the lower halls and Black Lake.

maps.title: The Stone Tooth
paragraphs: The map recovered from the Citadel led towards Durgeddin's lost stronghold beneath this landmark. Reaching the mountain meant exchanging Oakhurst's buried ruin for the orc-held approaches to Khundrukar.

maps.title: Above the streets, the bell tower
paragraphs: The bell tower overlooked Brindinford’s streets. It survived as a landmark even after the town below was ruined.

maps.title: Brindinford before its fall
paragraphs: The manor, temple and bell tower appear among Brindinford’s streets. The company would recognise those landmarks in the later sunken ruins.

maps.title: Brindinford · unmarked town plan
paragraphs: The first Brindinford adventure ended with the Baron freed and the city celebrating. This unmarked plan preserves that city’s streets, before the later volcanic collapse.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Brindinford's docks
paragraphs: Brindinford’s docks joined the early river routes. Those approaches later led towards ruins, the Deliverance and the passage beneath the earth.

maps.title: Pelor's temple in plan
paragraphs: These chambers formed Pelor’s temple, whose priests the conspiracy outlawed. The company fought to cleanse it and restore the sanctuary.

maps.title: Pelor's temple, room by room
paragraphs: Pelor’s temple is shown room by room. The company fought to restore this sanctuary for the priests and refugees of Brindinford.

maps.title: The manor on Silver Hill
paragraphs: The manor housed the Baron whose authority had been turned against Brindinford. The company fought its way inside to reach the mind flayer controlling him.

maps.title: The road between towns
paragraphs: The road from the early dungeons led to Brindinford. Its fair, temple and manor would become familiar stops in the company’s travels.

maps.title: Under the town's streets
paragraphs: Sewer bends run below the town’s streets. The company investigated concealed routes beneath Brindinford’s fair and public proclamations.

maps.title: Ways through the market
paragraphs: Brindinford's alleys could carry a crowd, a rumour, or an attacker out of sight. The fair made the town lively, while its narrow passages helped conceal the forces trying to seize it.

maps.title: Beneath Red Horse Hill
paragraphs: The chambers descend below Red Horse Hill. The tarn and its broken crystal connected Ossington’s troubles with Ashardalon’s missing heart.

maps.title: Ossington within the stones
paragraphs: Houses and fields stood inside Ossington’s double circle of stones. The company arrived with provisions and found Dyson’s experiments behind the village’s welcome.

maps.title: The Silence Keepers' stones
paragraphs: The circle marks the ancient Silence Keepers’ site. Ossington’s stones preserved duties and magic from before Dyson’s experiments.

maps.title: The island in the tarn
paragraphs: The island and crossing sit within the tarn. Nearby, the company sought answers from the Horseman about Dyson and the villagers.

maps.title: A closer plan of the first level
paragraphs: Numbered rooms fill the plan of the uppermost interior floor, just below the crown. The narrow eastern chamber is area 12, which the Brotherhood left unexplored.

maps.title: Another ring of chambers
paragraphs: Curved walls repeat around another floor of Nightfang. Behind its doors waited further creatures serving Gulthias.

maps.title: Below the tower's crown
paragraphs: The upper chambers stood within Ashardalon’s former temple. Gulthias preserved its undead cult alongside his own power.

maps.title: Nightfang, level by level
paragraphs: The plan continues through Nightfang’s guarded rooms. Grim found secret doors there and survived a pit trap with a prepared spell.

maps.title: The heat inside the tower
paragraphs: Fire and enclosed chambers formed part of Nightfang’s defences. The cult’s old rooms were being used to support Gulthias’s return.

maps.title: The room of Stitches
paragraphs: Tables, tools and scattered contents fill Stitches’s chamber. The room illustrates the flesh-working horrors within Gulthias’s domain.

maps.title: The tower's first floor
paragraphs: The first-floor plan shows Nightfang’s interior chambers. Traps, undead and hidden doors guarded the routes onward.

maps.title: A fortress below the surface
paragraphs: Guarded passages connect the chambers of this underground stronghold. The plan accompanies the war between the peoples of Deep Horizon.

maps.title: An underground village
paragraphs: Homes cluster among the underground growth. They show the settlements threatened by the war in Deep Horizon.

maps.title: Below the salamander citadel
paragraphs: The salamanders’ lower passages extend around the molten ground. They continued the defences beneath the upper citadel.

maps.title: Fire under Vesperian's shrine
paragraphs: Magma lay below Vesperian’s shrine. In Deep Horizon, the company had to cross and eventually divert the fire beneath the settlements.

maps.title: Paths through a green cavern
paragraphs: Pools and branching paths fill the green cavern. Settlements lay along such routes through the inhabited depths of Deep Horizon.

maps.title: The Underdark connections
paragraphs: The Underdark papers preserved a diagram of linked places and figures. Read it beside Helkitrin’s account of the mines, the captives and the forces threatening the desmodu.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: The salamanders' upper stronghold
paragraphs: Lava lights the salamanders’ upper citadel. Its defended chambers supported their assault on the desmodu enclave.

maps.title: The shrine above the magma
paragraphs: Vesperian’s shrine stood within the desmodu realm. Its chambers place the company’s discoveries within the enclave’s religious and civic life.

maps.title: The temple dungeon
paragraphs: The temple’s chambers lie in darkness beneath the earth. The company’s pursuit of Dyson and his companions continued into the underground expedition.

maps.title: Across the cube's faces
paragraphs: The map spreads out Kolyoral’s faces. Its cube-shaped terrain surrounded the company’s approach to the Iron Fortress.

maps.title: Brindinford on another map
paragraphs: Brindinford appears on a map within the fortress chapter. Other maps placed hostile forces near the town while Team Biscuit crossed the planes.

maps.title: Kolyoral, unfolded
paragraphs: The cube’s faces were mapped before the company entered the Iron Fortress. This unfolded reference belongs beside the other plans of Kolyoral.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Rigus at the edge of Acheron
paragraphs: Rigus opened the way into Acheron. After its fall, refugees fled to the Red Keep and fought to hold it.

maps.title: Routes through Acheron
paragraphs: Maps from the company’s Acheron road were linked into this route diagram. The lines connect the individual plans and crossings.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: The Outlands and the gates beyond
paragraphs: The ring of gate-towns places Rigus on the Outlands map. Its gate opened into Acheron.

maps.title: The battle for Brindinford
paragraphs: The marked map places forces around Brindinford. Hostile armies threatened the town while the company travelled across the planes.

maps.title: The next enclosure
paragraphs: Further walls and gates divide the approach. The company crossed defended ground on its way to the imprisoned smiths.

maps.title: The passage grows darker
paragraphs: Broken stone narrows the approach to the defended ruin. The image accompanies the passages the company crossed on its fortress expedition.

maps.title: The wheel of the planes
paragraphs: A mysterious planar diagram lay among the campaign’s maps and papers. It offers a reference for the planar roads that opened around the company’s journey through Rigus.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Walls on the road to a greater fortress
paragraphs: Walls enclose the defended courtyard. The illustration accompanies the company’s route from Rigus towards Imperagon’s fortress.

maps.title: Within the stone defences
paragraphs: Routes and rooms run within the stone defences. They illustrate the strongholds encountered on the planar expedition towards Imperagon.

maps.title: Zandikar, ground level
paragraphs: Zandikar became Terry’s stronghold after Imperagon fell. The Armor of Zandikar tied its gates and golem guardians to the planar forge.

maps.title: Zandikar, upper level
paragraphs: The upper plan extends through Zandikar’s rooms. Terry gained these chambers with the fortress after defeating its former master.

maps.title: Baldur's Gate on the wider map
paragraphs: Baldur’s Gate appears on the coast map. The Sleeper investigation ranged across familiar places while displacing the company in time.

maps.title: Beneath the Guild of Sleep
paragraphs: These chambers lay below the Guild of Sleep. The investigation led from them towards the Sleeper, the Time Stone and the company’s own past.

maps.title: Grimble's rooms
paragraphs: Grimble’s furnished rooms hold books, belongings and a table. They show the home the scholar could return to between expeditions.

Revisionist: Echoes in the Abyss borrowed Grim’s childhood home to make Xanthar seem like family. This artwork illustrates that borrowed setting; no map of the dream has been recovered. Grim’s profile links to the complete ordeal.

maps.title: Shoomma's smithy
paragraphs: Shoomma and Horken’s workrooms held the smithy’s tools and equipment. The company invested there during its return to earlier Brindinford.

maps.title: White Plume · Aquarium and Prison
paragraphs: The mountain’s challenge led through chambers built to test more than swordplay. This aquarium-and-prison handout preserves another plan from White Plume.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: White Plume · Geysers and Chains
paragraphs: Chains, water and dangerous crossings divided the hunt beneath White Plume Mountain. This handout plan records one part of Keraptis’s dungeon.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: A frozen map fragment
paragraphs: The northern handouts preserved this fragment of icy rooms. It belongs among the maps accompanying the company’s passage through Icewind Dale.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Luskan by its bridges
paragraphs: Luskan’s river and bridges appear on the coastal weapons trail. The Arcane Brotherhood’s interests reached towards the northern spire and its corrupted inhabitants.

maps.title: Neverwinter on the road north
paragraphs: The map places Neverwinter on the coastal hunt for Keraptis. Rumours about the stolen weapons pointed north towards the ice.

maps.title: The wider Faerûn
paragraphs: The map shows the wider reaches of Faerûn. Later journeys carried the company beyond them into Acheron and the Bastion’s plane.

maps.title: Brindinford's barracks
paragraphs: The barracks became hard-won ground when the two companies fought through the ant-held Sunken City. A building once tied to the town guard now offered a position from which exhausted survivors could consider the next advance.

maps.title: The Reality Wrinkle · later chamber
paragraphs: The Reality Wrinkle survived among Brindinford’s ruined streets and offered a passage onward. Its hidden trap caught Gravy, while Biscuit’s road led to Windglum.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Desayeus’s prison
paragraphs: Eco’s living doorway led into the prison where Desayeus held a fragment of the Soul Totem. Thunder carried the fragment out; the god remained bound.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Eco’s doorway
paragraphs: Eco guarded the only living entrance to Desayeus’s prison. The company sought divine permission to enter, with the prisoner’s chains expressly left beyond that permission.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: The Bastion’s approach
paragraphs: Ernie’s rings protected the companions as they crossed into the Positive Energy Plane. Beyond the approach waited the Bastion and the unborn souls sustaining Ashardalon.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: The Scaly Dog Inn
paragraphs: The Scaly Dog belongs to the company’s Windglum stopping places. The city sheltered the companions between the Wrinkle, Desayeus’s prison and the final crossing.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: The Wrinkle’s backroom
paragraphs: The old shop’s storeroom gave Biscuit shelter on the other side of its passage. From Windglum, Findula traced the route towards Eco and Desayeus.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Windglum
paragraphs: Biscuit reached Windglum after the companies parted at the Wrinkle. The companions returned here after leaving Desayeus’s prison, before travelling onwards to the Bastion.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: The mysterious prison plan
paragraphs: This annotated plan survives as a mysterious map among the campaign’s handouts. Its exact place in the company’s travels remains unresolved.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

maps.title: Zork’s great underground empire
paragraphs: A Zork map survives among the company’s puzzle papers. No surviving account places the companions in its rooms.
maps.credit: Artist and publisher credits remain on the original artwork where supplied.

groups.title: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

collectionNote: Town plans, dungeon floors and paths between worlds, with alternate views and the puzzling papers kept along the road. Reference sheets and unplaced plans carry their own labels.
